notes.claim: A function's derivative is zero where its graph has a horizontal tangent, at a turning point.
If a function has a local extremum at a point, that point is a critical point; a critical point is only a candidate and need not be a maximum or minimum.
On a closed interval, a largest or smallest value occurs either at an endpoint or at an interior point, where it is a local extremum and so at a critical point.
An HN engineering unit uses derivatives to locate turning points and to find the condition for maximum electrical power transfer.

sources.title: 4.3 Maxima and Minima - Calculus Volume 1 | OpenStax
sources.quote: In other words, local extrema can only occur at critical points.

sources.title: 4.3 Maxima and Minima - Calculus Volume 1 | OpenStax
sources.quote: Rather, it states that critical points are candidates for local extrema.

sources.title: 4.3 Maxima and Minima - Calculus Volume 1 | OpenStax
sources.quote: If an absolute extremum does not occur at an endpoint, however, it must occur at an interior point, in which case the absolute extremum is a local extremum.
